item.title: Lawyers in the pro-Palestine protestors case deliver closing statements
item.description: On Thursday, the trial of five pro-Palestine protestors arrested in June 2024 reached a final chapter. However, the jury has yet to begin deliberations. The post Lawyers in the pro-Palestine protestors case deliver closing statements appeared first on The Stanford Daily.

item.title: Newsom says: ‘Three strikes, four balls’
item.description: Accused of playing softball on crime, Governor Newsom announced a new plan to tackle crime in California... and beyond... The post Newsom says: ‘Three strikes, four balls’ appeared first on The Stanford Daily.

item.title: GSC debates OCS reform, ASSU bylaw amendments
item.description: The GSC expressed support for a student walkout and discussed OCS reform in light of the recent settlement between the family of Katie Meyer ’22 and the University. The post GSC debates OCS reform, ASSU bylaw amendments appeared first on The Stanford Daily.

item.title: Letter from the Editors: Vol. 269 begins
item.description: The Daily's new executive team introduces themselves and addresses the Stanford community regarding plans for The Daily's digital strategy, the ongoing lawsuit and goals for the new volume. The post Letter from the Editors: Vol. 269 begins appeared first on The Stanford Daily.

item.title: On the poverty of names
item.description: Our attempts to articulate the untranslatable are as futile as they are necessary, writes Baroudi. The post On the poverty of names appeared first on The Stanford Daily.

item.title: Stanford wrestling dominates Cal Poly in lopsided win
item.description: No. 16 Stanford routed Cal Poly 43-3, winning nine of 10 bouts in a bounce-back performance that reset the Cardinal’s momentum after an uneven stretch. The post Stanford wrestling dominates Cal Poly in lopsided win appeared first on The Stanford Daily.

item.title: Three books I couldn’t put down in January
item.description: In trying to accomplish her New Year’s resolution of reading for fun more, Audrey Chang ’28 reviews her three January reads: “If You Could See the Sun,” “Their Vicious Games” and “This Will be Funny Someday.” The post Three books I couldn’t put down in January appeared first on The Stanford Daily.

item.title: Women’s basketball struggles offensively in loss to Fighting Irish
item.description: Stanford women's basketball fell 66-78 to the Notre Dame Fighting Irish Sunday afternoon at Maples Pavilion. The post Women’s basketball struggles offensively in loss to Fighting Irish appeared first on The Stanford Daily.
